title: The Hacker Ethic: An Ethos Built Around Sharing and Teaching
explainer: Journalist Steven Levy's 1984 book Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution named and documented the 'hacker ethic' that grew out of MIT's Tech Model Railroad Club and early computer labs in the 1950s-60s: the belief that information should flow freely, that code should be shared and improved by whoever can make it better, and that people should be judged by skill rather than credentials. That ethos, more than any single tool, is the direct ancestor of today's security community's emphasis on public write-ups, conference talks, and mentoring newer researchers instead of hoarding knowledge.
